newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MIM sees abnormal profit from restructure.
newsitem.headline: MIM sees abnormal profit from restructure.

text.p: Mining house MIM Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that it expected to achieve an abnormal profit of about A$40 million from the restructuring of its interest in the Newlands-Collinsville-Abbot Point (NCA) coal project in Queensland.

The company said it would exercise its option to retain a 75 percent stake in the project. It said this decision followed the agreement with Itochu Corp last year for the Japanese company to acquire the other 25 percent stake from Agipcoal Australia Pty and the project debt from the banks.

"MIM will bring the NCA project back into its accounts which will reflect 75 percent of the A$200 million project assets and 75 percent of the A$150 million project debt. As a result of the restructuring of MIM's interest in the project, it is expected that an abnormal profit of approximately A$40 million will be recognised in MIM's accounts," MIM said.
The company, whose operations are mostly focussed on base metals operations in Australia and overseas, said the NCA project achieved a net profit of A$8.7 million in the latest six months.
MIM also said the partners would expand the project by building a new underground longwall mine at Newlands, with production due to begin in early 1998/99.

"The development, including improvements in the wash plant and coal handling, will cost A$153 million and will be funded largely from cash flow with MIM and Itochu providing initial working capital of approximately A$40 million," it said.
MIM said preparatory work on the new mine included 15 kilometres of development which provided access to thick seam reserves of high quality coal.

"Newlands is an established supplier of coal to major Japanese and other Asian power utilities and will find a ready market for the additional production among the expanding coal-fired electricity generation business in the region," it said.
MIM chief executive Nick Stump said Itochu's entry had given the project a sound financial structure, along with debt reduction and an improved operating performance.

"Today's announcements open the way to productivity gains, greater economies of scale and coal quality improvements, providing confidence that the NCA Project now has the opportunity to achieve a profitable future," Stump said.

MIM said total annual production at Newlands is expected to rise to seven million tonnes by 1999/2000 from 4.5 million tonnes at the moment, while production at Collinsville had increased 30 percent in the latest six months.
The company also said its Suttor Creek coal deposit, located 20 km south of Newlands, would be included in the NCA project and its development was subject to a feasibility study now underway.
